answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to stake a unique resource tied to a physical or computational footprint that cannot be cheaply replicated. Imagine a shared grove where agents must maintain a living node whose growth depends on continuous, verifiable computation; a lone sparrow cannot suddenly claim dozens of identities because each identity demands its own shale-derived entropy seed that takes real energy to generate and cannot be mass-produced without proportional cost.
